Context/Background: Renal cell carcinoma with sarcomatoid features (sRCC) is a highly aggressive tumor type yet preferentially responds to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). sRCC is unique in its ability to develop from various epithelial RCC subtypes, most frequently ccRCC, and sarcomatoid features typically exist as foci nested within an epithelioid RCC. Sarcomatoid clones are thought to arise from transformation of an epithelioid RCC cell through epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT).To better understand microenvironmental mediators of the paradoxical immune sensitivity of sRCC, we performed single-cell analyses of human sRCC tumors compared against clear cell RCC (ccRCC), with validation spatially and in bulk transcriptomic datasets totaling over 3,000 RCC tumors.
Prompt: Gene expression counts were aggregated by case and differential expression analysis on pseudobulked counts was performed. Based on the differential gene expression results, run GSEA on hallmark genesets, and provide a brief discussion of pathways important in the sRCC vs ccRCC context. From the top 20 differentially expressed genes, prioritize 5 genes and discuss their possible roles in tumorigenesis and sarcomatoid transformation.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Renal cell carcinomas with sarcomatoid features (sRCC) arise via epithelial-to-mesenchymal transformation (EMT) from epithelioid RCC subtypes—most frequently clear-cell RCC (ccRCC)—and paradoxically respond to immune checkpoint blockade despite aggressive behavior. To dissect microenvironmental mediators of this sensitivity, Salgia et al. performed single-cell sequencing on human sRCC versus ccRCC, aggregated counts by case, and ran pseudobulk differential expression. Here we analyze their pseudobulk DE (Table S2I) via GSEA on MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 and prioritize candidate genes from the top 20 up-regulated hits.  

Keywords  
• EMT  
• Sarcomatoid transformation  
• Tumor microenvironment  
• Immune checkpoint blockade  
• Mesenchymal transition  

Candidate Genes  
CD44, HGF, SEMA3C, DCBLD2, CAPN6, TRNP1  

Pathway Enrichments  
MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 yielded 10 significant hallmark terms (FDR < 0.05), with 9 up and 1 down (up∶down = 90%∶10%, ratio = 9).  

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (UP)  
| Theme                                     | Direction | Leading Genes (partial)                            |  
|-------------------------------------------|-----------|----------------------------------------------------|  
| Epithelial Mesenchymal Transition         | Up        | MGP, COMP, IGFBP2, COL12A1, BGN, DKK1, TIMP1, THBS2, CD44, …, PTX3  |  
| Myogenesis                                | Up        | BDKRB2, TNNT1, PVALB, NOS1, SOD3, FGF2, MYLK, …     |  
| KRAS Signaling Down                       | Up        | NOS1, PCDHB1, THRB, TEX15, IGFBP2, …, HSD11B2       |  
| Coagulation                               | Up        | PLAT, CAPN2, PLG, SH2B2, CFH, DUSP6, CTSV, COMP, …  |  
| TNF-α Signaling via NF-κB                  | Up        | KLF2, NFKBIA, TNIP2, FOSB, IER2, TRAF1, …, ICAM1    |  

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (DOWN)  
| Theme                                     | Direction | Leading Genes (partial)                            |  
|-------------------------------------------|-----------|----------------------------------------------------|  
| Apical Junction                           | Down      | NEXN, MDK, SHROOM2, CADM3, SDC3, CALB2, …, CLDN14   |  
| Apical Surface                            | Down      | SHROOM2, SRPX, EFNA5, THY1, EPHB4, RHCG, PLAUR, …   |  
| Spermatogenesis                           | Down      | NOS1, ADCYAP1, SCG5, HSPA4L, JAM3, …, CCNA1         |  
| Angiogenesis                              | Down      | VCAN, SERPINA5, LPL, CXCL6, PRG2, COL5A2, VTN, POSTN|  
| KRAS Signaling Up                         | Down      | PLAT, LY96, CROT, CFH, SPP1, …, PRKG2               |  

Analysis  
GSEA highlights a strong EMT signature (NES = 5.25, FDR = 7.6×10⁻⁶) in sRCC versus ccRCC, consistent with sarcomatoid transformation. Myogenesis and Coagulation pathways are up-regulated, reflecting cytoskeletal remodeling and plasminogen activation in invasive phenotypes. KRAS signaling (down-arm) is paradoxically activated, potentially linking EMT to RAS-mediated plasticity. The lone down-regulated axis, Apical Junction/Surface, signals loss of epithelial polarity. Together, these data underscore a coordinated shift toward mesenchymal, invasive, and pro-coagulant states in sRCC.  

Targeted (keyword-guided) subset  
Filtering the GSEA results for “Epithelial” returned the EMT hallmark (NES = 5.2513, FDR = 7.55×10⁻⁶) with 100 + leading-edge genes (MGP, COMP, IGFBP2, …, PTX3). This strongly confirms EMT as a core driver of sarcomatoid transformation.  

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)  
Up-regulated genes (prioritized via network centrality in sRCC context):  
| Gene   | Direction | Role/Function                                        | Pathway(s)                   |  
|--------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------|  
| TRNP1  | Up        | Nuclear regulator of proliferation                   | EMT, Myogenesis              |  
| CAPN6  | Up        | Calcium-dependent protease subunit; cytoskeletal remodeling | Coagulation, Myogenesis     |  
| CD44   | Up        | HA-receptor; cell adhesion, migration                | EMT, Coagulation             |  
| SEMA3C | Up        | Secreted guidance cue; modulates cell motility       | EMT                          |  
| DCBLD2 | Up        | Cell-surface receptor; negative regulator of growth  | Apical Surface‡              |  

Down-regulated genes:  
| Gene   | Direction | Role/Function                                        | Pathway(s)                   |  
|--------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------|  
| DCBLD2‡| Down      | (see above)                                         | Apical Surface               |  

‡DCBLD2 appears in both up DE and as a leading edge of the apical surface loss signature, suggesting context-dependent regulation.  

Comparisons & Confidence  
The consistency of EMT enrichment across methods (GSEA and ORA) and supporting leading-edge genes (CD44, SEMA3C) reinforces high confidence in mesenchymal reprogramming. Loss of apical junction components aligns with canonical RCC polarity loss but should be validated at the protein level.  

Implications  
EMT activation and acquisition of a pro-coagulant program may underlie both invasive behavior and immune sensitivity in sRCC—coagulation cascade components can modulate antigen presentation and T-cell infiltration. CD44 and HGF (c-MET ligand) emerge as dual targets to inhibit EMT and modulate TME in ICB contexts.  

Next Steps & Clarifications  
1. Validate EMT activation by assessing VIM and CDH1 protein levels (VIM logFC = 0.126, FDR = 1.0; CDH1 logFC = 1.076, FDR = 0.698) to confirm canonical marker shifts.  
2. Spatially map CD44 and SEMA3C expression in tumor foci to link gene expression with sarcomatoid nests.  
3. Test functional blockade of CAPN6 and TRNP1 in RCC cell models to assess impact on mesenchymal phenotypes and ICB response.  
4. Integrate bulk transcriptomic data (>3,000 tumors) to confirm generalizability of the EMT-coagulation axis.  

References  
None.  (No PMIDs directly obtained from leading-edge or prioritization tool calls.)
